recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. No core follow-up is needed unless a later work-group decision changes token :not behavior or adds a broader single-query OR mechanism for missing date values.
issue_request: FHIR-36646 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core-search. It requested explicit language that a missing SearchParameter element path does not match ordinary searches and that ne means the element has a value that is not equal to the specified value.
initial_application: Commit 13b8634a1423459eecdad6f69bc4f45b735cba44 applied FHIR-36646 to source/search.html by adding value-present wording to search prefixes and an explicit paragraph that prefix-based tests against non-existent elements fail, with missing-value searches requiring the missing or token not modifier.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes on 2022-04-04 record the approved clarification as ne not applying to missing values. Zulip implementation discussion clarified that the token :not modifier intentionally includes resources with no matching token value and is therefore not equivalent to ne. Later source edits for prefix terminology and examples reorganized the table but retained the missing-element rule.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html defines :missing true/false, states that token :not includes records without the searched token value, and explicitly says prefix-based tests against non-existent elements fail.

related_jiras.note: Later source/search.html prefix terminology cleanup changed the wording around resource and parameter values without changing the missing-element rule.
Later source/search.html prefix examples and comparison clarifications retained the FHIR-36646 missing-element paragraph.

evidence_items.learned: This explains why the current source correctly mentions the token-specific not modifier while still saying prefix tests fail on absent elements.
